text: $\lim _{x\to 0}\mathrm{cosec}x\left (\sqrt{2\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x}-\sqrt{\cos ^{2}x+\sin x+4}\right )$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $x=0$ both square roots equal $\sqrt{5}$. Rationalising:

$\mathrm{cosec}x\left (\sqrt{2\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x}-\sqrt{\cos ^{2}x+\sin x+4}\right )=\frac{\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x-4-\sin x}{\sin x\left (\sqrt{2\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^{2}x+\sin x+4}\right )}$

Here $\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x-4=(\cos x+4)(\cos x-1)=-2(\cos x+4)\sin ^{2}\frac{x}{2}$ and $\sin x=2\sin \frac{x}{2}\cos \frac{x}{2}$, so

$\frac{\cos ^{2}x+3\cos x-4-\sin x}{\sin x}=-\frac{(\cos x+4)\sin \frac{x}{2}}{\cos \frac{x}{2}}-1\to 0-1=-1$

The bracket in the denominator tends to $\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{5}=2\sqrt{5}$, so the limit is $-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: The product of all the rational roots of the equation $\left (x^{2}-9x+11\right )^{2}-(x-4)(x-5)=3$, is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve the given equation, start by rewriting the expression:

$(x^{2}-9x+11)^{2}-(x-4)(x-5)=3$

First, simplify the second part of the expression:

$(x-4)(x-5)=x^{2}-9x+20$

Now the equation becomes:

$(x^{2}-9x+11)^{2}-(x^{2}-9x+20)=3$

Introduce a substitution for simplification:

$\text{Let}t=x^{2}-9x$

Thus, the equation transforms to:

$t^{2}+22t+121-t-20-3=0$

Simplify further:

$t^{2}+21t+98=0$

Factor the quadratic:

$(t+14)(t+7)=0$

This gives:

$t=-7\text{or}t=-14$

Address each case where $t=x^{2}-9x$:

$x^{2}-9x=-7$

$x^{2}-9x+7=0$

Solving this quadratic equation, we find the roots:

$x=\frac{9\pm \sqrt{81-4\times 7}}{2}=\frac{9\pm \sqrt{53}}{2}$

$x^{2}-9x=-14$

$x^{2}-9x+14=0$

Solving this quadratic equation:

$x=\frac{9\pm \sqrt{81-4\times 14}}{2}=\frac{9\pm \sqrt{25}}{2}$

$x=\frac{9\pm 5}{2}=7\text{or}x=2$

The rational roots from the second equation are 7 and 2. Thus, the product of all the rational roots is:

$7\times 2=14$

text: Let $f(x)=\frac{2^{x+2}+16}{2^{2x+1}+2^{x+4}+32}$. Then the value of $8\left (f\left (\frac{1}{15}\right )+f\left (\frac{2}{15}\right )+\ldots +f\left (\frac{59}{15}\right )\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{4\cdot 2^{x}+16}{2\cdot 2^{2x}+16\cdot 2^{x}+32}=\frac{4(2^{x}+4)}{2(2^{x}+4)^{2}}=\frac{2}{2^{x}+4}$

Replacing $x$ by $4-x$:

$f(4-x)=\frac{2}{\frac{16}{2x}+4}=\frac{2^{x}}{2(2^{x}+4)}$

so $f(x)+f(4-x)=\dfrac{4+2^{x}}{2(2^{x}+4)}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $\frac{k}{15}+\frac{60-k}{15}=4$, the terms pair as $f\left (\frac{k}{15}\right )+f\left (\frac{60-k}{15}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$ for $k=1,2,\ldots ,29$, leaving the middle term $f\left (\frac{30}{15}\right )=f(2)=\frac{2}{8}=\frac{1}{4}$.

$8\left (29\times \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\right )=8\times \frac{59}{4}=118$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: If $α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation $2z^{2}-3z-2i=0$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $16\cdot \mathrm{Re}\left (\frac{α^{19}+β^{19}+α^{11}+β^{11}}{α^{15}+β^{15}}\right )\cdot \mathrm{Im}\left (\frac{α^{19}+β^{19}+α^{11}+β^{11}}{α^{15}+β^{15}}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dividing $2z^{2}-3z-2i=0$ by $2z$, each root satisfies

$z-\dfrac{i}{z}=\dfrac{3}{2}$

Squaring, with $i^{2}=-1$:

$z^{2}-2i-\dfrac{1}{z^{2}}=\dfrac{9}{4}\Rightarrow z^{2}-\dfrac{1}{z^{2}}=\dfrac{9}{4}+2i$

Squaring again:

$z^{4}-2+\dfrac{1}{z^{4}}=\dfrac{81}{16}+9i-4\Rightarrow z^{4}+\dfrac{1}{z^{4}}=\dfrac{49}{16}+9i$

This holds for both $z=α$ and $z=β$. Since $α^{19}+α^{11}=α^{15}\left (α^{4}+\dfrac{1}{α^{4}}\right )$, and similarly for $β$:

$\dfrac{α^{19}+β^{19}+α^{11}+β^{11}}{α^{15}+β^{15}}=\dfrac{\left (α^{15}+β^{15}\right )\left (\frac{49}{16}+9i\right )}{α^{15}+β^{15}}=\dfrac{49}{16}+9i$

The real part is $\dfrac{49}{16}$ and the imaginary part is $9$, so

$16\times \dfrac{49}{16}\times 9=441$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: $A$ and $B$ alternately throw a pair of dice. A wins if he throws a sum of 5 before $B$ throws a sum of 8 , and $B$ wins if he throws a sum of 8 before $A$ throws a sum of 5 . The probability, that A wins if A makes the first throw, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For one throw of a pair of dice, a sum of 5 comes from $(1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1)$, so $P(S_{5})=\dfrac{4}{36}=\dfrac{1}{9}$; a sum of 8 comes from $(2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2)$, so $P(S_{8})=\dfrac{5}{36}$.

A wins on his $k$-th throw when the first $k-1$ rounds (A's throw, then B's throw) produce no winner and A then throws a sum of 5. One round with no winner has probability

$\left (1-\frac{1}{9}\right )\left (1-\frac{5}{36}\right )=\frac{8}{9}\times \frac{31}{36}=\frac{62}{81}.$

Summing the geometric series,

$P(\text{A wins})=\frac{1}{9}+\frac{62}{81}\cdot \frac{1}{9}+\left (\frac{62}{81}\right )^{2}\frac{1}{9}+\cdots =\frac{\frac{1}{9}}{1-\frac{62}{81}}=\frac{1}{9}\times \frac{81}{19}=\frac{9}{19}.$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Consider the region $R=\left \{(x,y):x\leq y\leq 9-\frac{11}{3}x^{2},x\geq 0\right \}$.
The area of the largest rectangle of sides parallel to the coordinate axes and inscribed in R , is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
R lies above the line $y=x$, below the parabola $y=9-\dfrac{11}{3}x^{2}$ and to the right of the y-axis. For $x\geq 0$ the line rises and the parabola falls, so a rectangle $[x_{1},x_{2}]\times [y_{1},y_{2}]$ lies in R exactly when $x_{1}\geq 0$, $y_{1}\geq x_{2}$ and $y_{2}\leq 9-\dfrac{11}{3}x_{2}^{2}$; its area is largest with $x_{1}=0$ and both of the other conditions as equalities.

With the right side at $x=t$, the rectangle has corners $(0,t)$, $(t,t)$, $\left (t,9-\dfrac{11t^{2}}{3}\right )$ and $\left (0,9-\dfrac{11t^{2}}{3}\right )$.


[IMG]

$A(t)=t\left (9-\dfrac{11t^{2}}{3}-t\right )=9t-t^{2}-\dfrac{11}{3}t^{3}$

$A^{'}(t)=9-2t-11t^{2}=-(11t-9)(t+1)$

For $t>0$, $A^{'}(t)>0$ when $t<\dfrac{9}{11}$ and $A^{'}(t)<0$ when $t>\dfrac{9}{11}$, so the area is largest at $t=\dfrac{9}{11}$:

$A=\dfrac{9}{11}\left (9-\dfrac{11}{3}\cdot \dfrac{81}{121}-\dfrac{9}{11}\right )=\dfrac{9}{11}\cdot \dfrac{99-27-9}{11}=\dfrac{9}{11}\cdot \dfrac{63}{11}=\dfrac{567}{121}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Let $S_{n}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{20}+\ldots$ upto $n$ terms. If the sum of the first six terms of an A.P. with first term -p and common difference p is $\sqrt{2026\mathrm{S}_{2025}}$, then the absolute difference between $20^{\text{th}}$ and $15^{\text{th}}$ terms of the A.P. is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the value of $S_{2025}$, calculate the partial sum

$S_{n}=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{2025}\frac{1}{n(n+1)}=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{2025}\left (\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+1}\right )$

This series is telescopic, meaning most terms cancel out with each other:

$=\left (\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{2}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right )+\cdots +\left (\frac{1}{2025}-\frac{1}{2026}\right )$

Simplifying the expression, we find:

$=\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{2026}=1-\frac{1}{2026}=\frac{2025}{2026}$

Now, evaluate $\sqrt{2026\cdot S_{2025}}$:

$\sqrt{2026\cdot \frac{2025}{2026}}=\sqrt{2025}=45$

For the arithmetic progression with the first term $-p$ and common difference $p$, the sum of the first six terms is given by:

$\frac{6}{2}[-2p+(6-1)p]=3(3p)=9p$

Given that:

$9p=45$

We find:

$p=5$

To determine the absolute difference between the $20^{\text{th}}$ and $15^{\text{th}}$ terms of the A.P., compute:

$|A_{20}-A_{15}|=|(-p+19p)-(-p+14p)|$

Substituting the value of $p$:

$=|18p-13p|=|5p|=5\times 5=25$

Thus, the absolute difference is $25$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Let A be a $3\times 3$ matrix such that $\mathrm{X}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{AX}=\mathrm{O}$ for all nonzero $3\times 1$ matrices $X=\left [\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right ]$. If $\mathrm{A}\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 4 \\ -5 \end{array}\right ],\mathrm{A}\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 4 \\ -8 \end{array}\right ]$, and $\det (\mathrm{adj}(2(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{I})))=2^{α}3^{β}5^{γ},α,β,γ\in N$, then $α^{2}+β^{2}+γ^{2}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $X^{T}AX=0$ for every $X$, every coefficient of the quadratic form vanishes: $a_{ii}=0$ and $a_{ij}+a_{ji}=0$. So $A$ is skew-symmetric; let

$A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & a & b \\ -a & 0 & c \\ -b & -c & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$A(1,1,1)^{T}=(1,4,-5)^{T}$ gives $a+b=1$, $-a+c=4$, $-b-c=-5$.

$A(1,2,1)^{T}=(0,4,-8)^{T}$ gives $2a+b=0$, $-a+c=4$, $-b-2c=-8$.

So $a=-1$, $b=2$, $c=3$, and

$A+I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 \end{array}\right ],|A+I|=1(1+9)+1(1+6)+2(-3+2)=15$

$|2(A+I)|=2^{3}\times 15=120$. For a $3\times 3$ matrix $M$, $|\mathrm{adj}M|=|M|^{2}$, so

$\det (\mathrm{adj}(2(A+I)))=120^{2}=2^{6}\cdot 3^{2}\cdot 5^{2}$

Thus $α=6$, $β=2$, $γ=2$ and $α^{2}+β^{2}+γ^{2}=36+4+4=44$.

Hence, the answer is 44.

text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function such that $2(x+2)^{2}f(x)-3(x+2)^{2}=10\int\limits _{0}^{x}(t+2)f(t)dt,x\geq 0$. Then $f(2)$ is equal to $________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \text{Differentiate both sides} \\ \begin{array}{l} 4(x+2)f(x)+2(x+2)^{2}f^{'}(x)-6(x+2)=10(x+2)f(x) \\ 2(x+2)^{2}f^{'}(x)-6(x+2)f(x)=6(x+2) \\ (x+2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-3y=3 \\ \int \dfrac{dy}{y+1}=3\int \dfrac{dx}{x+2} \\ \ln (y+1)=3\ln (x+2)+C \\ (y+1)=C(x+2)^{3} \\ f(0)=\dfrac{3}{2}(\text{put}x=0\text{in the given equation}) \\ f(2)=19 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: The number of 3 -digit numbers, that are divisible by 2 and 3 , but not divisible by 4 and 9 , is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
No. of 3 digit numbers $=999-99=900$

No. of 3 digit numbers divisible by 2 & 3 i.e. by 6

$\frac{900}{6}=150$

No. of 3 digit numbers divisible by 4 & 9 i.e. by 36

$\frac{900}{36}=25$

$\therefore$ No. of 3 digit numbers divisible by $2&3$ but not by $4&9$

$150-25=125$
